threat_event: Ransomware delivered by a phishing email spreads across the flat office network to the gas control desk workstations, taking away the controllers' main SCADA screens and leading the Owner to order a precautionary shut-in of the line
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Gas control desk on the flat office network with email and web browsing; RMM agent on the desk; no awareness training; antivirus only, alerts in business hours; no incident response plan
sp800_53_controls: SC-7; CM-7; SI-3; SI-4; IR-8; AT-2
regulatory_driver: 49 CFR 192.615(a)(6); 49 CFR 192.605(c)(1)(iii); C-ENERGY-R03 (readiness reference only; SD 02G III.D.4)
existing_controls: MSP patching and antivirus; office firewall; mechanical regulators hold delivery pressure without SCADA
treatment_plan: Dedicated gas control desk workstations on their own firewall segment with no email; clean spare SCADA laptop kept off the network; MSP-managed EDR with alert monitoring; awareness training with phishing simulations; P08 runbook with the operate-or-shut-in decision table

threat_event: Attacker signs in to the hosted SCADA web client with a stolen or guessed password and sends valve commands or changes set-points
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: SCADA web client reachable from the internet; shared desk login; no MFA on any SCADA account; command rights from any device; browser-saved passwords on controller laptops; no sign-in alerts
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-031, G-032); C-ENERGY-R03 (readiness reference only; SD 02G III.C.2)
existing_controls: Vendor account lockout; role-based access (only controller accounts can command); RCVs fail to last position
treatment_plan: Vendor app-based MFA on every SCADA account; named desk accounts replace the shared login; sign-in alerts to the Owner and Operations Manager; remove saved passwords; monthly review of the command log

threat_event: Compromise or failure of the hosted SCADA vendor's platform or support tools affects the company's tenant and field devices
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single SCADA provider; vendor support staff enter the tenant without notice; no security or incident notice terms in the contract; company holds no copy of its configuration
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-024, G-025); C-ENERGY-R03 (readiness reference only; SD 02G III.F.1.a-d)
existing_controls: Vendor SOC 2 Type 2 controls (reviewed 2026-09-04, P09); manual operation by field staff
treatment_plan: Contract amendment: 24-hour security incident notice, notice of support sessions, 30 days' notice of changes; quarterly configuration export; manual operation call list tested each year

threat_event: Compromise of the MSP's RMM tool gives an attacker command execution on every company computer, including the gas control desk
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: RMM agent on all computers including the gas control desk; MSP security practices never reviewed; no SOC 2 report from the MSP
existing_controls: MSP states MFA on its console (not evidenced)
treatment_plan: Annual MSP security questionnaire with evidence; desk remote sessions only with Operations Manager approval; 24-hour incident notice and a recovery time for the gas control desk in the MSP contract

threat_event: During a cyber event the company shuts in the line when it did not need to, or keeps operating on SCADA data it should not trust, because no decision criteria exist
threat_source: Lack of decision criteria during a cyber event
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Emergency plan and abnormal operation procedures do not address cyber events or loss of trust in SCADA; no incident response plan; no rehearsal
regulatory_driver: 49 CFR 192.615(a)(6); C-ENERGY-R04 (192.631(a)(2)); C-ENERGY-R03 (readiness reference only; SD 02G III.F.1.d)
existing_controls: Emergency plan for physical emergencies; manual operation by field staff
treatment_plan: Cyber annex to the emergency plan with the P08 operate-or-shut-in decision table; tabletop with the MSP, SCADA vendor, and municipal system

threat_event: A former employee or contractor uses a SCADA account that was not removed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: SCADA removal depends on memory; departed Pipeline Technician active 5 months (disabled 2026-07-23); shared desk password known to former staff until 2026-07-23
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-031); C-ENERGY-R03 (readiness reference only; SD 02G III.C.4)
existing_controls: Account disabled and shared password changed 2026-07-23; audit log showed no use after departure
treatment_plan: Last-day checklist covering SCADA, suite, accounting, the interstate pipeline portal, keys, and padlock combinations; monthly SCADA user review by the Owner

threat_event: Attacker exploits a known vulnerability in RTU, flow computer, or gateway firmware
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Firmware versions unknown and never updated; no advisory tracking
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-029, G-038); C-ENERGY-R03 (readiness reference only; SD 02G III.E)
existing_controls: Carrier private network; no public addresses by design
treatment_plan: Field device inventory with firmware versions; monthly check of vendor and CISA ICS advisories; firmware updates under the O&M change procedure

threat_event: Cellular carrier outage removes telemetry from all 7 field sites at once
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One carrier for every site; no radio or second-carrier path
existing_controls: Abnormal operation procedure for loss of communications (technicians dispatched); mechanical regulators
treatment_plan: Second-carrier SIMs at the receipt station and the municipal gate station

threat_event: SCADA configuration or RTU programs cannot be rebuilt after loss, corruption, or tampering
threat_source: Vendor platform failure, tampering, or laptop loss
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Company holds no export of its SCADA configuration; RTU programs only on the Operations Manager's laptop
existing_controls: Vendor tenant backups and version history
treatment_plan: Quarterly configuration export and RTU program copies on encrypted media in the office safe; compare against the vendor history after any incident

threat_event: Hurricane damages the office and field sites and cuts power and communications for days
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single office; field sites depend on commercial power and one carrier
existing_controls: Emergency plan covers natural disasters; hosted SCADA reachable from anywhere; RTU battery backup
treatment_plan: Hurricane checklist: controller laptops and the spare laptop leave with staff before landfall; hotspot plan; pre-staged fuel and gauges at the gate station

threat_event: An on-call controller, tired after repeated night alarm callouts, misses or mishandles an alarm
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Night callouts not counted toward hours-of-service; fatigue education last given 2023; one person on call for a full week
existing_controls: Hours-of-service limit for business hours; on-call rotation among 3 controllers
treatment_plan: Count callout time toward hours-of-service; rest rule after more than 2 night callouts; annual fatigue education; record deviations (192.631(j)(2))

threat_event: Business email compromise leads to a fraudulent payment change or a false nomination message
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No awareness training; payment change requests accepted by email
existing_controls: MFA on email and accounting
treatment_plan: Call-back rule for any payment or banking change; nomination changes confirmed by phone with the interstate pipeline's scheduling desk; awareness training

threat_event: Leak-detection alerts mislead the on-call controller: false alerts cause alarm fatigue, or a quiet model gives false reassurance during a real leak
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Trial switched on by the vendor without validation, procedures, or approval; alerts go to the on-call phone
existing_controls: Controllers told verbally that the alerts are advisory
treatment_plan: Conditions in P10: alerts limited to the gas control desk until validated; written rule that SCADA alarms and field checks remain primary; validation and false-alert targets

threat_event: The SCADA vendor changes the platform, displays, or alarm behavior without notice and a controller misreads the change
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No notice term for vendor releases; leak module switched on without approval
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-024, G-037)
existing_controls: Vendor release notes published on its portal
treatment_plan: Contract term for 30 days' notice of changes; Operations Manager reviews release notes monthly and briefs controllers

threat_event: Staff do not recognize or report a cyber event, so the one-hour NRC clock, customer notices, or insurer notice are missed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident reporting rule for cyber events; no training
existing_controls: Emergency plan assigns NRC notices to the Operations Manager
treatment_plan: POL-03 reporting rule on a card at every desk and in each truck; covered in annual training; tabletop

threat_event: Records and maps in the productivity suite cannot be restored after deletion or encryption
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Suite backup keeps 30 days and has never been restore-tested
existing_controls: Nightly backup by the MSP; printed O&M manual and emergency plan in trucks
treatment_plan: First restore test; 90-day immutable versions; quarterly restore tests recorded

threat_event: A lost or stolen controller laptop or field tablet is used to reach SCADA
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Browser-saved SCADA passwords on 2 of 3 controller laptops; no MFA
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption; MSP can wipe laptops
treatment_plan: Remove saved passwords; SCADA MFA (R-002); report lost devices at once (POL-03)

threat_event: Someone breaks into an unstaffed field site and tampers with an RTU through its local port
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Unstaffed sites; local configuration ports inside the cabinet
existing_controls: Fenced and padlocked sites; locked cabinets; regular patrols (192.705); SCADA door-open alarms at 4 sites
treatment_plan: Accepted: physical barriers, patrols, and door alarms are proportionate for these sites; residual risk Low

threat_event: An outage of the hosted SCADA platform or the office internet line leaves controllers without SCADA beyond the 2-hour RTO
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Vendor stated RTO 4 hours; one office internet line; no clean spare device
existing_controls: Controller laptops on phone hotspots; manual operation
treatment_plan: Cellular failover router at the office; manual operation call list for hours 2 to 4 of a vendor outage; vendor RTO raised at contract renewal

threat_event: FPSC inspection finds the control room management fatigue and deviation records incomplete
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Fatigue education records missing for 2024 and 2025; no deviation records; callout time not recorded
existing_controls: CRM procedures (2019); hours-of-service records for business hours
treatment_plan: Close the 192.631 gaps in P03 (G-005 to G-008, G-014, G-015)

threat_event: Pipeline maps, SCADA screenshots, or network details shared by email or open file links help an attacker plan
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No classification rule; maps shared with contractors by open links
regulatory_driver: None binding; C-ENERGY-R03 (readiness reference only; SD 02G IV.B)
existing_controls: Suite sharing settings default to internal
treatment_plan: POL-04 classification; remove open links; share maps with contractors only through named access

threat_event: Employee personal information in payroll or HR files is exposed
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: HR files in the suite and payroll service
existing_controls: MFA on suite and accounting; payroll service security
treatment_plan: Accepted: few records, MFA in place, notice duties in the P08 matrix; residual risk Low

threat_event: Attacker on the internet reaches the cellular gateway at the municipal gate station and changes its routing or logs in to the RTU behind it
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Replacement SIM installed May 2026 was provisioned with a public address; gateway still had the manufacturer default password (found in P07 testing)
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-031, G-039); C-ENERGY-R03 (readiness reference only; SD 02G III.B.2)
existing_controls: Carrier moved the SIM to the private network 2026-08-19; password changed the same day
treatment_plan: Check all 7 SIMs against the carrier's private-network list; change every gateway and field device default password; SIM changes go through the O&M change procedure
